title: 0.3 while loops
objectives: Write while loops that are guaranteed to end: a condition, a progress step that changes it, and a limit
Spot and fix infinite loops (missing increment, a condition that can never become False) and out-of-range reads
Use counters, += and break to build retry-until-valid and wait-until-settled loops with timeouts
Read NMEA lines one at a time until a valid GGA fix arrives, and give up cleanly after max_tries

predict.question: What does this print?
predict.why: The increment happens BEFORE the print, so the first value printed is 1. When count reaches 3, the condition 3 < 3 is False and the loop stops, so 4 is never printed. Always ask: what's the value at the first print, and what's the last value that still passes the condition?

predict.question: A countdown that steps by 2. What does this print?
predict.why: n goes 5, 3, 1, -1. The condition is only checked at the TOP of each pass, so the loop doesn't stop the instant n 'reaches' 0: it stops when the check n > 0 fails, and n has already gone to -1. (It does end, because n keeps decreasing. With `while n != 0:` it would skip over 0 and run forever.)

predict.question: What does this print?
predict.why: break leaves the loop immediately, before the i += 1 line. When i is 2, the if is True, break runs, and the rest of the body (and the loop condition) is skipped. The value of i stays 2.

visualizations.title: Trace: a PLC-style watchdog

props.code:
heartbeats = [True, False, False, True, False, False, False, True]
timer = 3
scan = 0
tripped = -1
while scan < len(heartbeats):
    if heartbeats[scan]:
        timer = 3
    else:
        timer -= 1
    if timer == 0:
        tripped = scan
        break
    scan += 1
print("tripped at scan", tripped)

visualizations.notice: Each pass through the loop is one scan cycle. Watch `timer` in the variables table: it counts down on every missed heartbeat and reloads to 3 when one arrives. The trip only happens after 3 misses IN A ROW, and break skips the final scan += 1.

predictFirst.question: The watchdog reloads to 3 on every heartbeat and counts down on every miss. On which scan does it trip, and what is `scan` when the loop ends?
predictFirst.reveal: It trips at scan 6. Scans 1 and 2 count the timer down to 1, but the heartbeat at scan 3 reloads it. Scans 4, 5, 6 count 2, 1, 0, so timer == 0 at scan 6, and break exits before scan += 1, so scan is still 6.

challenge.task: Write first_fix(lines, max_tries), which reads lines in order (at most max_tries, never past the end) and returns the first stripped GGA line with a real fix (7+ fields, quality field at index 6 not empty and not '0'), or '' on timeout; and settled_index(readings, threshold, needed), which returns the index where `needed` consecutive readings below threshold have been seen, or -1. The GGA field table is shown here for reference.

bug.bugType: off-by-one loop counter (starts at 1 and runs to n inclusive)
bug.report: Bench log: "Heading drifts slowly even when the robot sits still after calibration. With a calibration buffer of exactly n samples, startup crashes with IndexError." gyro_bias(samples, n) is supposed to average the FIRST n gyro samples to estimate the bias. Find the bug and fix it.

explainBack.prompt: In your own words: what three things does every while loop need so it's guaranteed to end correctly? Use your first_fix loop as the example, and explain what would go wrong if you removed the `i < len(lines)` part of the condition.
rubric: Names a condition that is checked before every pass, plus a progress step in the body (i += 1) that eventually makes it False; without the progress step the loop never ends
Explains the limits: max_tries bounds the waiting time, and i < len(lines) prevents reading past the end (IndexError) when no fix ever arrives
Explains the early exit (return or break) on success, and how the code after the loop tells success from timeout (returning '' when nothing was found)

challenge: For first_fix, you need an index that moves forward one line per pass, and TWO reasons to stop: you've used up max_tries, or you've run out of lines. For settled_index, you need a counter that remembers how many low readings you've seen in a row, and something that resets it.

first_fix: loop while i < max_tries AND i < len(lines). Inside, strip the line, move i forward, and only look at field 6 after checking it's GGA and has at least 7 fields (a truncated line from power-up doesn't). Return the line as soon as it passes; after the loop, return ''. settled_index: on each reading, add 1 to the run if it's below the threshold, otherwise set the run back to 0; when the run equals needed, return the current index.

first_fix: i = 0; while i < max_tries and i < length of lines: line = strip(lines[i]); i += 1; if line starts with '$' and line[3 to 6) is 'GGA': fields = split(line); if there are at least 7 fields and field 6 is not '' and not '0': return line. After the loop: return ''. settled_index: run = 0; i = 0; while i < length of readings: if readings[i] < threshold: run += 1, else: run = 0; if run == needed: return i; i += 1. After the loop: return -1.
bug: Write down the indexes the loop actually reads when n is 4. Which index does a list start at? Which index is the last one in a 4-item list?
The counter starts at 1, so samples[0] is skipped, and `<=` makes it read samples[n], one past the first n. Start at 0 and loop while i < n: that reads exactly indexes 0 to n - 1.
